svg.title: the framework guards what reaches the repository: clean commits and no secrets: the full scan skips the libraries under vendor/ and still blocks a password in the project's own code
svg.text: the framework guards what reaches the repository: clean
Scenario: the full scan skips the libraries under vendor/ and still blocks a password in the project's own code

g.text: Given a generated project holds the same made-up password in its own src/ and in a library
A project generated from the toolbox. vendor/acme/mailer stands for a library that Composer, the PHP package manager,
installed there, and one of its test files holds a made-up password. The developer wrote the same line in
When the developer runs the full secret scan, it blocks src/mailer.php and skips vendor/
The full scan reads every file of the project. It finds the password in src/mailer.php, line 2, prints "REDACTED" where
the value was, and fails: "❌ Betterleaks detected secrets in your code!".
The same line under vendor/ is not reported: "leaks found: 1".
Then the scan's config lists vendor/ and tells a project allowlist to stand on its own,
The file every scan of the project reads. Its allowlist, the list of paths the scan skips, names '''(^|/)vendor/''' with
the other folders that hold no code of the project's own.
Above [extend], it says how a project adds paths of its own: copy this file whole, then point TASK_BETTERLEAKS_CONFIG
and REPOSITORY_BETTERLEAKS_CONFIG_FILE at the copy. It also says "Never point `[extend] path` at this file": MegaLinter
already wraps this file, betterleaks follows two extends at most, and the MegaLinter scan would load no rule and pass.
